name: EdgeBench
abstract: EdgeBench measures how agents learn from real environments over ultra-long horizons: 134 real-world tasks across six domains, each supporting 12 or more hours of continuous operation. Performance follows a log-sigmoid law in interaction time (R² = 0.998) — the benchmark behind the environment-learning scaling law.
contributions: 134 expert-built real-world tasks spanning science and ML, systems engineering, optimization, professional knowledge work, formal math, and games; experts averaged 57.2 hours per task.
Every task supports 12+ hours of agent operation, with extended runs beyond 72 hours; 51 tasks are public and 83 held out against contamination.
The SForge harness isolates the agent's work container from ephemeral judge containers, giving granular feedback in a closed improvement loop.
method: Agents work in an executable environment, submit repeatedly, and receive pass rates and failing-test feedback until timeout.
The best submission across the run is the task score.
Across ~38,000 hours of interaction, score follows a log-sigmoid function of environment time; learning speed roughly doubles every three months across model generations.

metrics.name: Score @12h
metrics.note: Best-submission score after 12 hours of environment interaction, averaged over tasks.

leaderboard_note: Published snapshot of the public task set; a full run is compute-intensive, so coverage grows slowly.
